newsitem.title: USA: SIA,PSA fault proposed customer communication rule.
newsitem.headline: SIA,PSA fault proposed customer communication rule.

text.p: A securities and bond industry group each told the National Association of Securities Dealers that proposals to curb brokers from telling customers misleading information are unworkable.

The groups, PSA, the bond market trade association, and the Securities Industry Association, separately told the NASD's regulatory arm that its rules are not needed because current safeguards are in place.
They said last week in letters to NASD Regulation Inc that the proposals would deter brokers from providing customers with information.

PSA complained in its August 12 letter that the proposal would subject brokers to "a variety of content requirements that have traditionally been applied only to mass communications with the public, such as advertising and sales literature.
"The proposed amendment would unnecessarily inhibit the use of electronic communications media," PSA said.
Under the proposal, letters and e-mail to individual customers would be subject to the same standards set for firms when they distribute advertisements and other information to multiple customers.
"We believe the amendments are unnecessary and would subject individual communications to inappropriate and unworkable standards," SIA wrote in its August 11 letter to NASD.

NASD's regulatory group proposed the rules because it is difficult for officials there to bring fraud cases against brokers who give misleading or unwarranted information to individual customers, an official said.

"To bring a fraud case you have to prove a lot of things. The advantage of having some more objective standards is that you can make sure that people are not making misleading or unwarranted statements," said John Ramsay, Deputy General Counsel of NASD Regulation.
"All you need to do is show that the standard is not met," Ramsay said.
Even so, Ramsay said NASD Regulation is "open-minded" about industry concerns and will likely address them when the proposals go before the NASD board later this year.
